references.text: Hagar flees into the wilderness for the first time and meets God's angel, which mirrors her later experience in the wilderness with Ishmael.
God hears the boy's cry and sends an angel to comfort Hagar and open her eyes to see a spring of water—the direct answer to her despair.
Judah says he cannot bear to see the disaster that would befall his father—parallel to Hagar's 'let me not watch the child die'.
Hannah weeps bitterly in her distress and prays to the Lord, paralleling Hagar's weeping over her child's fate.
God hears the cry of the helpless and does not despise their prayers, just as God heard Ishmael's and Hagar's cries.
Job 27:9 asks whether God hears in distress, while Genesis 21 gives the concrete answer: God hears and intervenes for those who call out.
